instruction: Extract and save the complete audio from the video as an MP3 file called 'Baby Justin Bieber.mp3' on the Desktop using VLC media player.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting complete audio from video and saving as MP3. Evaluator checks: (1) file exists (50% score), (2) audio duration is reasonable - between 60-400 seconds (50% score). The getter attempts to get duration using ffprobe on the VM; if unavailable, estimates from file size. Expected range allows for typical music video lengths while ensuring the audio wasn't truncated or corrupted.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: file existence, correct filename/location, and complete audio extraction
Getter logic is sound: uses ffprobe (preferred) with fallback to file size estimation for duration extraction
Metric correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('min_duration') and expected.get('max_duration') without incorrect patterns
Duration range [60-400 seconds] is semantically appropriate for typical music video lengths, preventing truncated or corrupted audio files
Partial credit scoring (50% file exists + 50% duration valid) is reasonable and provides granular feedback
The logic will work correctly at runtime - getter can extract state, metric can compare correctly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor enhancement (optional): Could add explicit MP3 format validation by checking file magic bytes, though duration check is a strong proxy for successful extraction
